summary: @servicetitan/contentful ships preinstall dropper that fetches Bun runtime and executes 727 KB obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (hex identifiers, string-map indirection) and at npm install time downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts the bun binary to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727 KB heavily obfuscated JavaScript payload (numeric string-shuffle array of ~2000 entries, rotation function, custom decode alphabet — the standard shape of a packed obfuscator). Invoking the payload through Bun bypasses Node-only tooling and executes attacker-controlled code on the installer's host at package install time. The package advertises itself as 'Shared components for working with contentful' (a React/UI library) and has no legitimate reason to fetch an alternate JavaScript runtime or execute an obfuscated sibling module. The @servicetitan scope, repository pointer to github.com/servicetitan/anvil-uikit-contrib, and 'contentful' name are consistent with impersonation of the ServiceTitan organization.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
